title: pm-dispatch: a held epic child and a waiting card thread leave a machine-readable mark, and the patrol reads it (two misses 2026-11-21)
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXU3aQQzivgaDDU82c

Filed at the maintainer's ask on 2026-11-21. Verbatim and untranslated: 「为什么会出现疏漏？技能哪里有问题」 (22:48Z). Standing project instruction: where the skill is wrong, open a card to fix it.

## What happened

1. **Epic children never dispatched after their blocker closed.** #35890 (epic #35590) was held "after #35853", and #35892 "after #35878 / #35876 / #35702". The order lived in a coordinator comment and in the seat's project memory. Neither card carried a `Blocked-by:` line, and both stayed `pm:queue`. #35878 closed at 06:03Z and #35853 at 10:48Z. Nothing re-read the two cards until the maintainer asked at 14:01Z, which cost 8 h and 3 h.
2. **A card thread and its seat waited on each other for 15.5 h.** PR #35923 (#35897 + #35899) pushed merge commit `473c7ff4` at 06:47Z. Its thread ended its turn on "report the head to the seat when CI is green". #35977 had merged at 06:19Z, so the PR was already in conflict. GitHub starts no `pull_request` workflow on a conflicting PR, and that head has zero GitHub Actions check suites. No green event and no red event ever came, so the subscription never woke the thread, and the seat was waiting for the thread's report. A resume thread picked it up at 22:2xZ, and #35901 / #35902 wait on it.
3. **Claims without the label write (13 cards).** The seat posted `Claim:` comments through `post-stamped.mjs` instead of one `label-write.mjs --comment-file` stroke (`execution-duties.md` 70). The cards stayed `pm:queue` with no assignee until triage knocked. Fixed at 08:5xZ.

## Where the skill is at fault

- `references/filing-gate.md` 20 says a same-epic order preference is listed on the epic card. That is prose with no reader. It contradicts `references/seat-lifecycle.md` 56: order is written only as the child's `Blocked-by:`. Only a `Blocked-by:` line feeds the unlock scan, `card-pick.mjs` and H19.
- `references/execution-duties.md` 48 says a card behind an unmerged blocker is not opened as a thread. It does not say the seat writes `Blocked-by:` + `pm:blocked` in the same stroke as that decision. So the hold can live only in memory.
- `references/seat-lifecycle.md` 90 asks for `card-pick.mjs --order … --why` only when the seat reports an empty queue. A busy seat never reports empty, so it never ran the per-card pass over its epics' children.
- The seat post (#34366) was last edited 2026-11-20T03:41Z. Four epics and six areas were added after that, and its serial queue reads "None". `seat-post-protocol.md` 17-20 already requires a refresh, and H38 exists, but the patrol did not run it.
- Card-thread liveness has no rule. `execution-duties.md` 176 probes only a dispatched dev. `dispatch-runbook.md` 105 counts only "IDLE and not pushed" as a stall. `dispatch-runbook.md` 115 checks check-suites only for the App-push case. Nothing asks a thread or a seat to confirm that CI started after a push. Nothing bounds a "report when green" wait.
- The only idle detector, `project-forms.md` 50 (open PR idle ≥3h → `Request: progress`), belongs to the triage seat on another account. In the script, H12 and H16 skip every draft PR (`check-half-states.mjs` `h16NeedsDetail` and the H16 predicate: `pr.draft !== false`). In this fleet, every card PR stays draft until the seat lands it, so the conflict detector is blind exactly where the work is.
- `post-stamped.mjs` accepts a body that opens with `Claim:`, so the one-stroke claim rule is not enforced.

## To do

Skill text (the draft PR from this thread):
1. `filing-gate.md` 20: the order between same-epic cards is the later card's `Blocked-by:` line, not a preference on the epic.
2. `execution-duties.md` 48: deciding "this waits for #N" writes `Blocked-by: #N` + `pm:blocked` on the card in the same stroke. ⛔ Never only in memory or a comment. A target merging then releases it through the existing scan.
3. `seat-lifecycle.md` 90: every patrol round runs `card-pick.mjs --order <序> --why` over the areas and epics the seat holds. A child with no hold reason is dispatched that round, or its reason is written on the card.
4. `dispatch-runbook.md` card-thread section: within 10 min after a push, the thread confirms that CI started and the PR is not `dirty`. If not, it merges `origin/main` and pushes again. Any wait on CI sets a fallback wake (`send_later`, ≤30 min). Each patrol round, the seat reads `pr-state.mjs` for every in-flight card PR. It wakes the thread that round on any of: zero Actions check suites 30 min after the head was pushed, `dirty`, or no push and no report for 2 h.
5. `execution-duties.md` 176: the status probe covers card threads as well as devs.

Scripts (separate PR, seat schedules):
6. `check-half-states.mjs` H12/H16: read a draft PR that carries a `Claim:` (an in-flight card PR) too, or add a row for "claimed draft PR: dirty, or head without Actions check suites, past N h".
7. `post-stamped.mjs`: refuse a comment whose first line opens `Claim:` and point to `label-write.mjs --comment-file … --add pm:dispatched --remove pm:queue --assign`.

## Acceptance

- A seat that follows the skill leaves no epic child on `pm:queue` with a closed blocker for longer than one patrol round. The hold is visible as `Blocked-by:` on the card, and `card-pick --why` names it.
- A card PR that is `dirty`, or whose head has no Actions run, is flagged within one patrol round, whether it is draft or not.
- `post-stamped.mjs --self-test` shows a `Claim:` refusal.
- `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` stays green. The skill-text PR raises ceilings only by a ruling's measured delta, or pays by deletion.

Reader: area:fleet (pm-dispatch skill text, scripts/pm).
